The house, on the ground

Open this on your phone at the site. It stands the design up at full size — house, decks, piles and garage — set out and levelled off natural ground, not the finished platform.

Orange = set-out · ticked line = zone 29 × 33 m

Checking whether this phone can do AR…


  


  


  

    
01Set out

    
The mark is the centre of the footprint rectangle — the small orange ring and cross. Let the phone walk you to it, or pace it from a boundary mark.

    

      
      

        —

      or open the mark in Maps →
    

    
Your blue dot and its accuracy ring show on the plan below, to scale. If the ring is bigger than the house, trust the tape, not the phone.

    
    
      
  1. 1
    Tape it instead if you prefer: from where the access spur meets the lot, 22.3 m on 192°; or from the east boundary corner, 25.5 m on 258°. Set a compass app to true north, not magnetic.
    2. 
      
  2. 2
    Tap “Stand it up at full size”, sweep the phone at the ground a couple of metres ahead until it locks onto a surface, then tap to drop the house.
    3. 
      
  3. 3
    Twist with two fingers until the orange arrow points true north. Everything else follows from that one move.
    4. 
      
  4. 4
    Orange on the ground, from heaviest to lightest: the three floor plates with a tick at each corner — those ticks are the pegs — then the decks, then the garage slab. The ticked green line is the zone boundary — flat on the ground plane here, draped over the landform on the second tab.
    5. 
      
  5. 5
    It spreads 29 × 33 m, which is more than phone AR holds steady. Place from the middle, work outward, and drop it again from the same mark when the ribbon stops matching the ground.
    6. 
    

    

      
The AR model carries no terrain. Its ground is one flat plane at natural ground under the set-out mark (RL −3.59), so heights read true near the mark and drift from reality as the real hill falls away. Section 04 is the correction.

      
Drive, lawn and retaining are on the second tab, not in the AR model — ground surfaces would fight the real ones. Interiors aren't visible either; the room volumes are solid massing.

04Floor against real ground

    
Levels are RL in the model's frame. Bed wing floor −3.25 (soffit −3.70) · link + living −4.35 (soffit −4.80) · garage −7.55 · lawn −4.50.

    

      

        
WhereNatural RLResult

        
          
Bed wing, north tip (master)−2.01cut 1.7 m

          
Bed wing, east wall−2.56cut 1.2 m

          
Bed wing, west wall−4.96pile 1.3 m

          
Bed deck, west edge−5.11pile 1.7 m

          
Living room, centre−5.13pile 0.3 m

          
Living, south-west corner−7.62pile 2.8 m

          
Wrap deck, west corner−8.14pile 3.6 m

          
Garage slab−6.62cut 1.1 m

        
      

    

    

      
Standing on the set-out mark, the bedroom floor should read about 0.3 m above your feet. Walk north-east and the ground climbs into a cut over head height at the master; walk south-west and the building lifts onto piles until the wrap deck is 3.6 m up.

      
If the model looks like it's resting on the slope rather than cutting into it uphill and floating downhill, the AR plane has locked at the wrong height — drop it again.
